title: Community Health Work
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 16S/24Q to fewer than 30S/45Q units

program.section_heading: Community Health Work - Certificate of Achievement: City
outcomes: Recognize, identify, assess, and address key concepts in aging (e.g., physical and mental health, exercise, nutrition, the normal aging process, etc.) affecting optimal aging and older adulthood functioning.
Identify and compare the various public benefits available through local, state, federal, public assistance programs.
Identify and make referral to appropriate services.
Recognize and identify risk of caregiver stress, particularly in caring for individuals suffering from Alzheimer's and other dementia.
Make a report of an incident or suspected incident of an abuse/ neglect of dependent adults and elders.

notes: HUMS 118 and PSYC 130 are required in the catalog but absent from the closed list; recorded as catalog additions.
The 18.0-21.0 unit range reflects HUMS 270 being variable at 1.0-4.0 units.
The department recommends a course sequence (HUMS 103 before HUMS 121; HUMS 121 before HUMS 122 or HUMS 270). This is sequencing advice for required courses, not a separate recommended-course list.

The printed learning outcomes focus on aging, caregiving and elder/dependent adult abuse reporting, which seem only loosely matched to a community health work certificate. They may have been carried over from another program; a reviewer should check them.
Career entry taken from the summary phrase 'utilize entry-level front-line health care workers'.
